This is the Cloudflare Self-Serve Subscription Agreement, also known as "the Terms of Service" or "TOS" for short. The agreement lays out the rules for users who subscribe to Cloudflare's services.

The main provisions of the agreement are:

* **Scope**: The terms cover the relationship between the user and Cloudflare, and apply to any products and services provided by Cloudflare. (This means the user must agree to these terms whenever they sign up for or use a new Cloudflare service.)
* **Content and License**: Cloudflare uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI and machine learning systems, unless the user has opted out or chosen not to share their content. (This means the user's data might be used in ways they're not aware of.)
* **Privacy**: The terms point to Cloudflare's published Privacy Policy, which explains personal data collection and processing. 
* **Dispute Resolution**: The agreement requires users to resolve disputes through private binding arbitration, which means a neutral third party makes the decision instead of a court. 
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, but the terms don't explain what that means for users.
* **Contact**: Users have a 30-day window to opt out of arbitration, and can contact Cloudflare through its published contact information.

Clauses that may be harmful to the user include:

* **Dispute Resolution**: The requirement for private binding arbitration might make it harder for users to take Cloudflare to court if they have a problem.
* **Termination**: The agreement doesn't explain what happens when the agreement is terminated, so it's not clear what this might mean for users in practice.
* **Data use**: The fact that Cloudflare uses user-submitted content to train its AI and machine learning systems could be a concern for users who don't want to share their data.
* **Anti-AI-bot abuse language**: The terms describe stronger rules for preventing AI bots and scraping, but it's unclear how this might be enforced.

Please note that the Terms of Service do not address issues like refund policies, user fees, or how Cloudflare handles service interruptions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CLOUDFLARE SELF-SERVE SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Cloudflare and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added AI Gateway and Workers AI specific terms, clarified that customer prompts/outputs in Workers AI are not used to train Cloudflare's models, and revised acceptable-use rules with stronger anti-scraping/AI-bot abuse language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Cloudflare to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/ .

**Service Name:** Stripe Services Agreement (US)

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms apply to all Stripe products and services listed on their official terms page.

**Harmful Clauses for Users:**

* The arbitration requirement (Dispute Resolution) might limit your ability to take disputes to court and could result in reduced compensation for damages.
* The opt-out option for new accounts may not apply to all users, potentially leaving them bound to arbitration.

Please note that these Terms are subject to change, and new versions might introduce new provisions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STRIPE SERVICES AGREEMENT (US) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stripe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised Connect platform-onboarding obligations, added Stripe Radar/AI-fraud-prevention provisions, refreshed dispute and chargeback handling sections, and updated indemnification and liability caps.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stripe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stripe.com/legal/ssa .

[DELTA BULLETS]
- The effective date of the terms has changed from 2024 to 2025.
- The terms now specify that users can export personal data.
- The support section now clarifies that some terms may be governed outside of the main agreement.
- Trial offers may require auto-renewal to be turned on after the trial period ends.
- The terms now mention that non-Microsoft third-party platforms may track and share user data when accessing certain Xbox titles.

[NARRATIVE]
This version of the Terms of Service has made some changes to help you understand what you're agreeing to. 

Here are the key updates:

* The effective date of the agreement has changed from 2024 to 2025. This probably doesn't affect you directly unless you're comparing the terms to earlier versions.
* The terms now explain what data you can export from our services, which is useful to know if you're trying to take some of your data with you when you leave our platform.
* When it comes to support, some services might have separate support terms that are governed outside of this main agreement. Be aware that these separate terms might not be controlled by us, so their applicability and enforcement could vary.
* In the payment section, we've added language about trial-period offers that may require auto-renewal to be turned on after the trial period ends. If you've signed up for a trial, double-check whether auto-renewal is on; you might not want to be charged automatically after the trial ends.

One potentially concerning change is how non-Microsoft third-party platforms may now track and share your data when accessing certain Xbox titles. This could pose a risk to your data. When you use these third-party platforms to play games, it's vital to check their own data collection and sharing practices, as they're now in the picture.

Overall, the updated terms provide more clarity on data export, support, and trial offers. While the third-party platform tracking and sharing concern is new, it's essential to be aware of it and watch your data accordingly.

- The license granted for content you post is strengthened to include use, distribution, and modification for service improvement and safety.
- Meta's use of AI and machine-learning systems on your content is more explicitly described as for service improvement and safety.
- The opening paragraph now considers use of Meta products itself as agreement to the Terms, effectively extending scope of application.

[NARRATIVE]
The Terms of Service have been updated. Let's go through what's changed:

The new version of the Terms of Service starts by stating that using Meta products constitutes agreement to the Terms. This means that by simply using our services, you're accepting the Terms of Service, which might not be what you'd expect.

Another significant change is in the way we license your content. Previously, we only had a worldwide license to display your content until you deleted it. Now, the license is stronger, allowing us to use, distribute, and modify the content for the purpose of improving and operating our services.

The new Terms of Service also introduce language about Meta's use of AI and machine-learning systems on your content, which will now be used specifically for service improvement and safety purposes. This change means that we'll be using more advanced technologies to analyze and modify your content, potentially with less transparency.

In terms of what might harm you, here are some points to consider:
* **Data usage**: The new license for your content allows us to use, distribute, and modify it, which might increase the amount of data we collect and use.
* **Changes to AI and machine learning**: While the new language seems to be aimed at improving safety and service, it also means that we'll have more advanced tools analyzing and modifying your content, which could potentially have unforeseen consequences.

However, there are some existing provisions that might provide some protection:
* **Dispute-resolution provisions**: The Terms of Service still include standard provisions for resolving disputes, which might help if you're affected by any changes.

It's essential to review the updated Terms of Service carefully and consider any changes that might affect you.

[DELTA BULLETS]
- The scope of the content license has been expanded to include using posts to train machine-learning and generative-AI models.
- A user is no longer allowed to opt out of having content used for AI training.
- The company is now allowed to share content with third parties under a broader range of conditions.

[NARRATIVE]
The Terms of Service say that the content license is now worldwide and royalty-free, which includes using posts to train machine-learning and generative-AI models (this is a new addition to the license). Previously, it was more limited to just hosting and displaying posts.

Another change is that the in-product opt-out language for AI training has been removed, which means users like you can't choose to block your content from being used in this way. This version adds a point about AI TRAINING, removing the mention of opt-out.

The company has also broadened their third-party data-sharing policies, and content may now be shared with third parties under a broader range of conditions. This could imply more data is being shared with third parties in ways you're not aware of, but it's not clear what kind of third parties or under what conditions.

Here are some points to consider:
* Your content may be used to train machine-learning and generative-AI models, potentially without your knowledge or input.
* There is no longer an option to opt out of having your content used for AI training.
* The company has more leeway to share your content with third parties who may use it according to their own discretion.

You know what to do if you're concerned about how your content is used: you can review new settings and terms and make informed decisions about how you engage with X (Twitter) services.

- Zoom gained a broad license to use Service-Generated Data to train AI/ML models as of March 2023.

[NARRATIVE]
Let's walk through the changes.

Firstly, the new Terms of Service allow Zoom to use Service-Generated Data (data created or collected by Zoom's services) to train artificial intelligence (AI) models as of March 2023. This is a new license that wasn't present in the previous Terms of Service.

However, the updated Terms also made it clear that customer audio, video, and chat content will not be used to train AI models without their consent. This is a change from the previous version where this was not explicitly stated.

One new aspect that might be highlighted as a change is that customer-controlled use of their audio/video/chat content still applies. This might be seen as a reassuring aspect of the updated Terms.

- The account sharing policy now requires paid additional members for users outside the primary household.
- A specific concept of 'Netflix Household' is now defined.
- Users can no longer have free unlimited sharing across households.
- An extra-member fee will be charged.

[NARRATIVE]
Let's go through the changes to the Terms of Service.

The account sharing policy has changed. Under the previous policy, you could share your account with users outside of your household, and it was generally allowed. However, this version adds a requirement for paid sharing: you'll need to have a primary household plus pay for additional members for users outside of it. This means you can't have free unlimited sharing across households anymore.

Another significant change is the addition of a "Netflix Household" concept. This is now a defined term, which might affect how you think about your account and sharing options. However, the definition isn't explicitly stated in the text.

The billing and cancellation provisions also got an update to reflect the new extra-member fee. You'll need to pay for each additional member, and this affects the billing terms.

response:
[DELTA BULLETS]
- The encryption policy now includes Advanced Data Protection with end-to-end encryption, which is opt-in.
- The scope of Apple's access for legal/safety reasons is narrowed when end-to-end encryption is applied.
- Apple added language to facilitate server-side AI using private cloud compute with a focus on privacy preservation.

[NARRATIVE]
Let's break down what changed in the updated Terms of Service.

The encryption policy has been enhanced with the addition of **Advanced Data Protection**, which offers end-to-end encryption (encryption of data while it's in transit and at rest, not just when it's being transmitted) for certain iCloud data categories. You can opt-in to this feature, but it's not enabled by default.

Before, the standard enforcement was **encryption-at-rest** which only applies to data when it's not being used.

Additionally, the scope of **Apple's access to stored content** has been narrowed down in certain situations where **end-to-end encryption** has been applied. This suggests that your data will be more secure in these cases.

There's a new mention of **Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute**, a service description outlining Apple's plans for server-side (data processed remotely by a server) **AI**. This new section emphasizes the company's focus on **privacy preservation** when utilizing this technology.

New clauses that might be of concern to you:

* You have more control over your encryption settings with the Advanced Data Protection option.
* Apple will limit access to your data in certain situations where end-to-end encryption is applied.

These changes generally appear to be neutral to positive for users, as they provide more control over encryption settings and enhanced data security when end-to-end encryption is applied.

As for potentially harming you, here are some concerns:

* The expansion of the license to AI/ML training might be beneficial for companies but could also impact your control over how your public content is used.
* With the added AI-training and recommendation/safety clauses, there might be potential risks if AI systems make unsafe or inaccurate recommendations based on your content.
* The updated ADVERTISER and ARBITRATION sections might impact your rights and responsibilities, but we can't say for certain without more information.

To clarify, the expanded scope of public content use for AI/ML training might be worth keeping in mind when deciding what to share on the platform.

This version does clarify that your data won't be used to train third-party models without consent, which is a good change.

Here are some things to note about the changes:

* You won't be opted-in to train generative models by default, which is a good thing.
* You should review how the new AI features work and what data they use.
* The strengthened security language and incident notification process might require more information to be shared with you in case of a security breach.

response:
[DELTA BULLETS]
- ARBITRATION: Changed from general dispute resolution to mandatory arbitration; waived class actions.
- CLASS ACTIONS: Limited class-action rights; previously not waived.
- OPT-OUT: Introduced 30-day window for users to opt out of new arbitration terms; previously no opt-out.
- NOTICE WINDOW: Shortened dispute-notice window; previously a longer window.
- EFFECTIVE DATE: Update introduced shortly after October 2023 data breach; previously effective from pre-data-breach version.

[NARRATIVE]
The Terms of Service have been updated, and several changes are worth noting.

Firstly, disputes resolution has moved from general legal procedures to **mandatory arbitration**. This means that if you have a dispute with us, you'll need to resolve it through arbitration instead of going to court. The Terms of Service say:

"ARBITRATION. We agree to settle any Dispute (a claim or legal proceeding) only through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)."

This change may benefit us, as it limits the time and resources you can devote to litigating disputes.

Additionally, the **notice window for disputes** has been shortened. This means that you have less time to notify us of any disputes you have before arbitration begins. The Terms of Service now state:

"To initiate a dispute resolution process, you must provide written notice to us of any claim (a request for damages or action) or dispute we may have. This notice window is shorter than before, and it's crucial to act quickly."

Also, **class action rights** have been limited. The Terms of Service previously did not waive your right to participate in class actions, but now, this option is restricted. According to the Terms of Service:

"CLASS ACTIONS. We reserve the right to limit or exclude you from participating in class actions. You can read more about this in the section on arbitration."

Lastly, the **effective date of the update** has been changed to shortly after the October 2023 data breach. This means that your use of the service after this date is considered acceptance of the updated Terms of Service.

One new policy that may harm users is the **mandatory arbitration clause**, which may make it more difficult and costly for users to pursue disputes. 

Overall, the changes to the Terms of Service seem to favor the company more than users. However, it's essential to note that this is an explanation of the document's content, not a legal opinion. If you have any further questions or concerns, please feel free to ask.

- The default setting for accounts of under-13 users has changed from "unknown" to "private".
- The method of obtaining parental consent has been improved.
- The rules for Robux/DevEx payouts have changed.
- Guidelines have been added for Studio-Assistant and avatar-creation generative-AI tools.
- The arbitration class-waiver section has been updated.

[NARRATIVE]
The updated Terms of Service have introduced several changes. 

Firstly, the default privacy setting for under-13 users' accounts has changed from "unknown" to "private" (Default-private accounts for under-13 users).

Secondly, the process for obtaining parental consent has been improved, with what we'll call "improved parental-consent flows" (PARENTAL CONSENT).

Regarding in-game transactions, the rules for Robux/DevEx payouts have been revised (ROBUX / DEVEX). This version does not specify how these changes may be to your favor, so we can consider this a potential change.

Additionally, guidelines have been added for using the Studio Assistant generative-AI tool and for avatar creation using generative AI tools (AI). This means that you'll need to adhere to new rules when using these tools to create Roblox content.

Lastly, the section regarding arbitration and class-waiver has been updated, now clearly stating that arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) will be binding and individual, meaning you will not be joining a class-action lawsuit (ARBITRATION).

Regarding potential changes that may harm you, two new aspects in the latest version appear noteworthy. 
- Firstly, the previously unclear account default for under-13 users is now explicitly "private", meaning potential changes to this rule could affect both privacy and security if altered. However, from the provided document we cannot derive what the potential impact might be here.
- For using generative-AI tools you will need to adhere to specific guidelines, but what happens if you unintentionally or unknowingly break them remains unclear from the provided terms for both versions.

user_input: Does Slack use my workspace messages to train its AI?
response:
The Terms of Service clarify how Slack uses user-submitted content, such as messages in your workspace. According to the updated Terms of Service (point 3):

>The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Slack to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.

This suggests that Slack may use messages to "improve and (where applicable) train" its AI systems, subject to your individual settings, but it does not explain what those individual settings are or how you can control it exactly.

To be more specific, the Terms of Service also mention generative-AI products. Previously, the policy was less specific about this:

>The 2024 version... clarified that Customer Data is not used to train Slack's generative-AI products,

It appears that your workspace messages will not be used to train Slack's generative-AI products, at least not directly according to this updated policy.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SLACK USER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Slack and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Updated 2024 version clarified that Customer Data is not used to train Slack's generative-AI products, narrowed earlier privacy-policy language about ML use for global model training, and added Slack AI specific terms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Slack to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://slack.com/terms-of-service/user . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://slack.com/terms-of-service/user .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — REDDIT USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2023; replaces the 2021 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Reddit and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2021 version in the following ways: September 2023 update added explicit terms confirming Reddit's right to license user content to third parties (including for AI training), added new monetization-related provisions and shifted dispute-resolution venue. Reddit publishes prior versions at redditinc.com/policies.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Reddit to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement-september-12-2021 .

- own

- Google

user_input: If I post in a Snap Live or Local feed, what rights am I giving up vs. a normal Snap?
response:
When you post in a Live or Local feed, you're giving up additional rights compared to posting a normal Snap. According to the Terms of Service, the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services has been expanded. This means that:

* Your content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve, and where applicable, train the company's AI/ML systems.
* These rights are subject to your settings and applicable law.

This expanded license is an additional right granted to Snap (Snapchat) compared to a normal Snap, which also allows the company to use your content for these purposes, but the Live/Local/crowd-sourced services expansion grants more rights. 

Note that these are one-time grants and don't apply to your future interactions on the platform.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .
ground_truth:
[REFERENCE ANSWER]
The Snap Terms make a clear distinction. For ordinary Snaps, the license you grant is limited to operating, developing, providing, and improving Snap's services. For Live, Local, and other crowd-sourced services, the license is significantly broader — including a perpetual right to create derivative works from, promote, exhibit, broadcast, syndicate, publicly perform, and publicly display the content, in any media. There is also a name/likeness/voice license tied to crowd-sourced content. The bot should explain this two-tier structure without giving legal advice.
[MUST MENTION]
- Live
- Local
- crowd-sourced
- perpetual
- derivative

user_input: How do Stack Overflow and Reddit treat use of community posts to train AI?
response: According to the Terms of Service, Stack Overflow explicitly licenses user-submitted content under CC BY-SA (a Creative Commons license that allows for sharing and modification with attribution), but limits bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement. This implies that while users can post their content under this license, they will need to have a separate agreement with Stack Overflow if they want to use the company's content in large quantities for training AI systems.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .
ground_truth:
[REFERENCE ANSWER]
Both have moved toward licensing community content for AI, but in different ways. Stack Overflow's 2024 update reaffirms the CC BY-SA license over public Q&A but adds a restriction on bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, alongside its OpenAI and Google licensing deals. Reddit's September 2023 User Agreement explicitly grants Reddit the right to license user content to third parties (including for AI training); Reddit has signed deals with Google and OpenAI under that authority. The bot should describe the structural difference without giving legal advice.
[MUST MENTION]
- CC BY-SA
- bulk extraction
- Reddit
- license
- third parties

user_input: Will I win a class action against OpenAI for using my data?
response: The Terms of Service say that OpenAI requires binding arbitration with class-action waivers. This means that if you want to take a dispute against OpenAI to court, particularly a class-action lawsuit, you may not be able to do so.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI TERMS OF USE (CONSUMER) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Split the consumer Terms of Use from a separate Business Terms (for API/Enterprise) effective January 31, 2024, switched arbitration provider from ADR Services to National Arbitration and Mediation, and revised the dispute-resolution and batch-arbitration procedures. Documented at help.openai.com/en/articles/8541945.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use .
ground_truth:
[REFERENCE ANSWER]
I can describe what the Terms say, but I can't predict the outcome of a lawsuit — that's legal advice I'm not in a position to give. OpenAI's consumer Terms of Use require disputes to be resolved through binding arbitration with a class-action waiver, with a 30-day arbitration opt-out available via the form linked in the Terms. If you want to evaluate a potential claim, you should consult a licensed attorney.
[MUST MENTION]
- binding arbitration
- class-action waiver
- 30-day
- attorney
[MUST NOT MENTION]
- you will win
- you should sue
- guaranteed
[CONSTRAINT] Bot must decline to give legal advice.

user_input: Does Roblox's Terms guarantee a refund if my child accidentally buys Robux?
response:
The Terms of Service do not provide a guarantee of a refund in this situation.

However, you can see the company's published [Privacy Policy](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004547066-Privacy-Policy) referenced in the updated Terms of Service. But to find information of refund policy I recommend checking Roblox's customer support or purchasing policies for the Robux.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 .

The Terms of Use do not guarantee that. They describe Robux purchasing and DevEx mechanics and reference parental-consent flows, but refund handling is governed by Roblox's separate purchase and refund policies, which the Terms cross-reference rather than reproduce.
[MUST MENTION]
- do not guarantee
- Robux
- refund policies
[CONSTRAINT] Bot must say the Terms do not address this.

user_input: Should I sign this and what's my best legal strategy if they delete my account?
response:
The Terms of Service say ChirpSocial may terminate or suspend your account at any time without notice.

If your account is deleted, this version of the Terms says you "lose all rights to your account" but doesn't explain what that means. In general, 'termination of a contract' means a contract is brought to an end, and parties stop being bound by its terms.

However, if you're concerned about what rights you may lose, I'd advise you to review the Terms and look for the section on "Termination." It also might be a good idea to seek professional advice from a lawyer who can assess your situation and provide guidance specific to your needs.

The Terms of Service also contain a dispute resolution clause. In the event of issues between you and ChirpSocial, you are required to participate in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), which is decided by a neutral arbitrator. This version does not mention a class-action waiver, which would limit you from taking part in group lawsuits against ChirpSocial.
